title: Same-spin correlation screens the exchange peak of the electron gas near 2kF
abstract: arXiv:2610.35896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exchange alone gives the electron gas a local field factor with a sharp peak just below 2kF. Quantum Monte Carlo finds none. Both spin channels are computed here from their lowest diagrams with a dynamically screened interaction and no fitting. Parallel spin correlation is the negative image of exchange and removes about half the peak; the calculated spin-resolved factors account for the QMC data at rs = 1 and 2, and at q = 0 for the compressibility and spin susceptibility obtained from the ground-state energy. The two classes of diagrams are the two terms of the kernel of Hedin's vertex equation, of which the second is routinely dropped.
summary:
- Exchange alone yields a sharp local‑field peak just below 2k_F, absent in QMC.
- Dynamically screened lowest‑order diagrams show parallel‑spin correlation cancels ~½ of the peak, reproducing QMC at rs = 1, 2 and q = 0 compressibility/spin susceptibility.
- The omitted second term of Hedin’s vertex kernel is essential for accurate spin‑resolved local‑field factors.

title: An exactly solvable obstructed seam on a lattice Klein bottle: bulk-locked Majorana rings and register-dependent toric codes
abstract: arXiv:2610.35931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a frustrated seam produced by literal reflection gluing of Wen's plaquette model on a closed lattice Klein bottle. The seam operators anticommute along two cycles for even circumference and one cycle of twice the length for odd circumference. Their algebra reduces to free Majorana rings, while the commuting bulk stabilizers constrain the allowed ring sectors. This bulk locking yields exact ground energies, excitation gaps and degeneracies, checked by phase-aware Pauli traces and finite-size diagonalization, including two 24-qubit energy predictions. The seam degeneracy is not topological: the single-site seam fields tested split it at second order. We contrast this obstructed gluing with consistent toric-code realizations. An edge register preserves the anyon labels; a Hadamard-dressed site register has colour-dependent seam transport, with ground-state degeneracy 2 or 4 for even circumference and a sign-frustrated exception at odd circumference. For the enumerated lattice isometries and sizes, we compute logical gates and distances, distinguishing abstract qubit relabelling from local hardware depth. Finally, on three 16- and 24-qubit lattices, chiral matter selects a holonomy doublet whose electric-field splitting follows two competing tunnelling routes. These matter results remain finite-size statements. The main result is the exact obstructed-seam solution with bulk sector locking; the register, gate and matter calculations delimit its relation to topological codes.
summary:
- Exactly solvable frustrated seam on a lattice Klein bottle reduces to free Majorana rings with bulk‑locked sectors.
- Ground‑state energies, gaps, and degeneracies are analytically obtained and confirmed by finite‑size diagonalization; seam degeneracy is non‑topological and split by single‑site fields.
- Register‑dependent toric‑code realizations and logical‑gate analysis show distinct ground‑state degeneracies and holonomy doublets on 16‑ and 24‑qubit lattices.

title: Agentic Swarms Discover Enhanchment of Fractional Chern Insulator Gaps Beyond Ideal Quantum Geometry
authors: Yitong Zhang, Changwen Xu, Andrew Boshi Li, Siddhartha Sarkar, Kai Sun, Venkatasubramanian Viswanathan
abstract: arXiv:2610.35934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can artificial intelligence (AI) move beyond solving well-defined problems to contribute to open-ended discovery in fundamental physics? Could AI propose what to explore, identify unexpected phenomena, and uncover their mechanisms? We address this using MOSAIC (Multi-agent Open-ended Scientific Analysis and Investigation through Collaboration), a collaborative swarm of AI agents (Claude Opus 5.5), to tackle a longstanding bottleneck: the small energy gaps limiting the robustness of fractional topological order and the study of anyons at higher temperatures. Rather than prescribing a model, we ask frontier models (GPT-6 Astra) to propose a theoretical framework, which MOSAIC explores through diverse strategies and rapid exchange of ideas. This reveals a striking finding: although ideal quantum geometry is considered favorable for fractional states, departing from this limit can dramatically enhance their robustness, with many-body gaps more than an order of magnitude larger than in the ideal case. Without centralized coordination, the agents explored autonomously, combined findings across agents, and formed insights from individual runs, outperforming isolated agents with the same tools. AI-assisted theoretical analysis further develops simplified models with an analytical gap enhancement factor that is unbounded within the single-band approximation. Remarkably, AI identifies the real-space quantum metric, rather than the momentum-space one, as the key quantity governing the many-body gap, revealing how flat-band wavefunctions shape two-electron interactions and yielding an index computable from single-particle wavefunctions without many-body ED to guide gap optimization. Our study demonstrates how collaborative AI agents can integrate exploration, discovery of unexpected physics, and theoretical understanding, opening new possibilities for AI-driven research in fundamental physics.
summary:
- AI swarm MOSAIC finds that moving away from ideal quantum geometry boosts fractional Chern insulator gaps by >10×.
- Autonomous, collaborative agents outperform isolated ones by jointly proposing, exploring, and synthesizing models.
- Derived an unbounded analytical gap‑enhancement factor tied to the real‑space quantum metric in the single‑band limit.

title: Planckian dissipation per unit critical entropy as a coupling-free probe of the strange-metal bath
abstract: arXiv:2610.35939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strange metals pair a resistivity linear in temperature with a specific heat $C/T$ rising logarithmically on cooling. We find that, if electrons scatter off a local critical bath, the coupling cancels in the ratio $Q$ of their coefficients, leaving two measurable numbers: how slowly the bath relaxes, seen in photoemission or optics, and the share of critical entropy that relaxes current. Baths form classes: $Q\le4.91$ for a conformal bath, as SYK models confirm; 9--15 for the Yukawa--SYK field; and far less for Kondo lattices. LSCO, at $Q\approx9$, exceeds the conformal bound, pointing to the Yukawa--SYK field.
summary:
- Strange metals exhibit linear‑T resistivity and logarithmic‑T specific heat; the ratio \(Q\) of their coefficients is coupling‑independent.
- \(Q\) is set solely by the bath’s relaxation rate and the fraction of critical entropy that relaxes current, with distinct ranges for conformal (\(\le91\)), Yukawa–SYK (9–, and Kondo baths.
- LSCO’s measured \(Q\approx9\) exceeds the conformal bound, pointing to a Yukawa–SYK critical bath.

title: Machine learning enabled design of sustainable alloys considering real world constraints
authors: Quan Li, Zhilong Wang, Lei Shi, Baojing Feng, Changhui Liu, Jie Wang, Jingya Wang, Weisen Zheng, Matic JovicevicKlug, Ziyuan Rao, Jinjin Li, Dierk Raabe, Xiaoqin Zeng
abstract: arXiv:2610.35946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing sustainable alloys must reconcile high performance with real-world constraints, including feedstock scarcity and variability, processing and energy requirements, regulatory thresholds, and economic limitations. Addressing these constraints reaches far beyond today's conventional performance-focused frameworks. It needs to consider not only complex property-processing-performance trade-offs but also sustainable production pathways. Here, we propose a physics-informed ensemble (PIE) learning framework that integrates fundamental structure-property relationships with processing routes and sustainability criteria for mechanism-based alloy design. It predicts properties from composition-microstructure relationships and infers processing routes under sustainability constraints, establishing an interdisciplinary approach to identifying sustainable alloy solutions. We validate the approach for Mg alloys, a lightweight yet energy-intensive metallic material class, considering performance, cost, and carbon emissions. Trained on a benchmark dataset, the PIE model systematically explores plausible alloy compositions and microstructures to construct a digital library of millions of candidate alloys. From this space, we identify two sustainable Mg alloy solutions that overcome the conventional performance-cost-emission trade-off: a rare-earth-containing alloy increases yield and tensile strength by 72.8 percent and 61.1 percent, respectively, over alloys from the same family at comparable cost and emissions; and a rare-earth-free alloy reduces cost and carbon emissions by 40.4 percent and 88.9 percent, respectively, relative to its primary-feedstock counterpart, without compromising mechanical performance. This work introduces a general, physics-informed, and quantifiable framework for designing sustainable alloys under real-world constraints.
summary:
- Physics‑informed ensemble learning framework that couples structure‑property, processing routes, and sustainability constraints for alloy design.
- Applied to Mg alloys, generating a digital library of millions of candidate compositions and microstructures.
- Identified a rare‑earth‑containing Mg alloy that increases yield and tensile strength by ~73 % and ~61 % while meeting cost and carbon‑emission targets.

title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.35973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed before a global average can be inferred with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ uniformly sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. The law of total variance exposes a second error, the floor $R_n$, which arises because the observed configuration is a single draw from equilibrium: no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle we derive $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$ and show that the posterior remains calibrated. At the critical point of the two-dimensional Ising model the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$; its mean-field limit is $\sqrt{2}-1$. For correlated fields read by sensor networks, the usual 95\% interval covers the ensemble mean in 7\% of cases. Bounding the floor from one realisation, as in single-chain Monte Carlo diagnostics, requires an assumption on the decay of correlations.
summary:
- Bayesian estimator of average displacement in random transposition shuffle has relative uncertainty \(1/\sqrt{2m}\), independent of deck size \(n\).
- A variance floor \(R_n=(2n^2+/(5(n-^2(n+)\) limits precision; the posterior remains calibrated.
- In the 2‑D Ising critical point, energy floor vanishes while magnetization floor ≈072 (mean‑field limit \(\sqrt2-1\)); sensor‑network intervals cover the ensemble mean only 7 % of the time.

title: Tunable turning point of the frequency--temperature response in suspended bilayer SiN_x/Al nanofilms
authors: Yanli Shi, Hui Wu, Guangyu Li, Zhuo Miao, Luyao Zhu, Chen Zheng, Weidong Zheng, Qun Cao, Zhe He, Zheng Cui
abstract: arXiv:2610.35977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-invasive thermometry is highly desirable in cryogenic experiments to avoid the self-heating inherent in conventional sensors. In previous work, temperature was probed via the vibrational eigenfrequency of a suspended single-layer SiNx nanofilm. However, the turning point of the frequency-temperature curve limited the usable measurement range. Moreover, the slow thermal response confined measurements to a stepwise protocol with only discrete temperature points. Here, we show that these limitations can be overcome with a suspended bilayer SiNx/Al nanofilm, whose temperature-dependent vibrational eigenfrequency provides a monotonic, continuous, and repeatable temperature readout. The frequency-temperature dependence is governed by the mismatch between the effective coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) of the bilayer and the substrate, which makes the turning point tunable through the thickness ratio of the two layers. Over the 90 K to 300 K range, we characterize three bilayer nanofilms with different Al layer thicknesses and show how the turning point shifts with the thickness of the Al layer. For the sample with 72 nm Al, the turning point is pushed beyond 300 K, yielding a monotonic negative temperature coefficient over the entire 90 K to 300 K range. Combining a thin Al layer on the SiNx film with improved thermal anchoring of the chip shortens the thermal response to below 1 s, enabling continuous frequency tracking at a ramp rate of 3 K/min. We also demonstrate that the nanofilm with a 72 nm Al layer achieves a repeatability better than 150 mK above 175 K, and the frequency resolution of 1 Hz corresponds to a temperature resolution of ~5 mK.
summary:
- Bilayer SiNx/Al nanofilms provide a monotonic, continuous temperature readout via vibrational eigenfrequency, eliminating the turning‑point limitation of single‑layer SiNx.
- The turning point is tunable by Al thickness; a 72 nm Al layer pushes it beyond 300 K, yielding a negative temperature coefficient over 90–300 K.
- Enhanced thermal anchoring shortens the thermal response to <1 s, enabling real‑time frequency tracking.

title: Cutting, Shuffling and Diffusion as a Coarsening Process
authors: Daniel Lester, Tanguy LeBorgne, Joris Heyman
abstract: arXiv:2610.35979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cutting and shuffling (CS) rearranges fluid without stretching, but homogenisation requires diffusion (D); this interaction is not well understood. We show that CSD is a coarsening process, with scale $\bar\ell=L(n_c\mathrm{Pe}/2)^{-1/3}$ rather than the Batchelor scale, and that cutting acts as a fractional Laplacian in wavenumber, giving the exact mixing rate $\gamma=2^{1/3}|a_1'|n_c^{2/3}\lambda\mathrm{Pe}^{-1/3}$ for $n_c$ cuts per event at rate $\lambda$, with $a_1'=-1.0188\dots$ the first zero of $\mathrm{Ai}'$. This holds in any dimension for random and deterministic protocols, extends to finite-time mixing, and places CSD in a known non-equilibrium universality class.
summary:
- Cutting‑shuffling rearranges fluid without stretching; diffusion is required for homogenisation.
- CSD coarsens with scale \(\bar\ell=L(n_c\mathrm{Pe}/^{-1/3}\), not the Batchelor scale.
- Exact mixing rate \(\gamma=2^{1/3}|a_1'|n_c^{2/3}\lambda\mathrm{Pe}^{-1/3}\) (with \(a_1'=-0188\ldots\)), valid in any dimension, for random or deterministic protocols, and finite‑time mixing.

title: Amorphization-Depth-Dependent Bismuth Redistribution and Activation in Silicon for Quantum Devices
authors: Youcef A. Bioud, Simon-Jean Michel, Sebastien Francoeur, Sjoerd Roorda, Eva Dupont-Ferrier
abstract: arXiv:2610.35993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-surface bismuth donors are promising for silicon quantum devices because of their rich electron-nuclear spin structure and long spin coherence, but their electrical activation is strongly influenced by implantation-induced amorphization. We compare redistribution and electrical activation of 20 keV Bi implanted directly into Si and after Si preamorphization. The two routes produce amorphous-layer depths of approximately 47 nm and 177 +/- 15 nm, respectively. After annealing at 650 C for 300 s, Rutherford backscattering spectrometry and channeling reveal comparable substitutional Bi fractions of 91 +/- 2% and 89 +/- 4%, whereas Hall measurements indicate Hall-derived electrical activation yields of approximately 60% and 90%, respectively. Depth-resolved ion-scattering analysis reveals a buried Bi-related feature at or beyond the initial amorphous/crystalline interface, within the end-of-range region, together with increasing surface segregation at higher annealing temperatures. The buried feature is consistent with trapping near residual end-of-range defects. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and low-temperature photoluminescence on the Bi-only sample reveal no resolvable Bi-oxide contribution and a donor-related optical signature, respectively. These results show that amorphization depth and regrowth geometry govern Bi redistribution and influence electrical activation beyond substitutional incorporation alone.
summary:
- 650 °C anneal yields ~90 % substitutional Bi, yet electrical activation is 60 % for shallow (47 nm) vs 90 % for deep (177 nm) preamorphization.
- A buried Bi feature at the amorphous/crystalline interface indicates defect trapping; surface segregation rises with higher annealing temperatures.
- XPS/PL show no Bi‑oxide and reveal donor‑related optical signatures, highlighting that regrowth geometry, not just substitutionality, controls Bi activation.

title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
abstract: arXiv:2610.36029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^\omega(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $\omega\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,\gamma,\epsilon)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $\omega_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $\omega$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD
summary:
- Open‑source GAP package **AlgebrasTQD** computes condensable algebras \(A(H,F,\gamma,\epsilon)\) for twisted quantum doubles \(D^\omega(G)\).
- Provides algebra structures, anyon content, isomorphism classes, twin algebras, subalgebra lattice, and Hasse diagram for any finite group \(G\) with 3‑cocycle \(\omega\).
- Enables reduced topological order, interface anyon maps, and construction of non‑Clifford logical gates in non‑Abelian surface codes.

title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
authors: Xuhao Jiang, Jad C. Halimeh, N. S. Srivatsa
abstract: arXiv:2610.36054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^{\alpha}$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $\alpha$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $\alpha$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.
summary:
- Krylov complexity is strongly suppressed and size‑independent in the strongly confined regime (small α, small transverse field).
- Oscillation frequencies of the complexity match meson masses; the dominant frequency scales linearly with the lightest meson mass, while the time‑averaged complexity scales as its inverse square.
- At finite temperature, operator Krylov complexity displays bounded oscillations that encode the meson spectrum at low T, which fade as temperature rises.

title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
authors: Zanya Gonzalez Tellez, Miguel Angel Oca\~na Bribiesca
abstract: arXiv:2610.36115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.
summary:
- Coulomb U and exchange J independently reshape γ‑Ce spectral correlations, invalidating a single U‑J effective parameter.
- Raising U shifts the strongest level repulsion across the 4f manifold; no monotonic Poisson→Wigner transition.
- Exchange J produces coexisting repulsive and clustered spectral regions within the same 4f manifold, despite unchanged total spin and occupation.

title: Three-dimensional quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlore systems
authors: Ze-Xun Lin, Robert-Jan Slager, Claudio Castelnovo
abstract: arXiv:2610.36199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2\pi/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $\sigma_{yz}=\sigma_{zx}=\sigma_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

title: A cascade of orbital-field-driven phases with a Lifshitz-type transition to unidirectional spiral order
abstract: arXiv:2610.36214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.
summary:
- Orbital‑field coupling on the honeycomb Heisenberg model creates a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order‑by‑disorder into a cascade of collinear magnetic phases.
- As the field increases, a Lifshitz‑type transition occurs to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that breaks chiral symmetry, with spin stiffness becoming negative along one direction.
- The transition is driven by coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped spin‑orbital fluctuations, yielding a spiral wavevector that grows as the square root of the distance from criticality.

title: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO
authors: Daniel Staros, Federico Petrovich, Ammar Kirmani, Daniel N. Blaschke, M. Cerezo, Jian-Xin Zhu
abstract: arXiv:2610.36268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising path towards efficient calculations of the electronic structure of correlated materials. The properties of iron-based materials, which are key for advancing geological and astrophysical understanding, are notoriously difficult to calculate with classical computers. However, despite the many recent advances in quantum computing on near intermediate scale quantum hardware, a full treatment of the electronic structure of high-$Z$ atoms or molecules remains challenging. Here, we investigate the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimental quintet ground state of FeO is recovered classically and with quantum algorithms, while a nonet ground state is recovered for Fe$_2$O$_2$. Although raw VQE does not achieve chemical accuracy for the ground state of FeO or Fe$_2$O$_2$, SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules utilizing remarkably few quantum computational resources. Overall, our results indicate that $ab \; initio$-informed low-energy models of correlated materials, combined with SQD, offer a new alternative for scaling up calculations of ground-state properties of strongly correlated solids on existing quantum hardware.
summary:
- SQD with two connectivity shells exactly reproduces FeO and Fe₂O₂ ground‑state energies using few qubits.
- Classical diagonalization and VQE recover FeO’s quintet ground state; VQE lacks chemical accuracy.
- Suggests ab initio‑informed low‑energy models + SQD as a scalable method for correlated solids on near‑term hardware.

title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
authors: Cole Kelson-Packer, Hiroki Sukeno, Akimasa Miyake
abstract: arXiv:2610.36528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gauge-Higgs theory in flat spacetime provides a prime theoretical model of multiple phases of matter with distinct entanglement structures. More recently, there has been interest in hyperbolic space and the influence its extensive boundaries have on these structures. Entanglement transitions between non-equilibrium phases, such as topological phases, can be realized by the competition of non-commutating measurements. Here we study the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices described by measurement-only dynamics. We chart 2D phase diagrams by employing topological entanglement entropy and introducing a generalized measurement-induced entanglement tailored for hyperbolic Higgs phases. Utilizing duality, we find a phase absent in Euclidean space, wherein the bulk lattice hosts separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order. Transitions between this "archipelago" phase and neighboring topological and trivial phases feature a critical exponent $\delta$ belonging to a mean-field universality class. Our essential tool is a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation that simulates the spacetime evolution of the 2D quantum state with a third direction of entanglement. This allows us to analyze spacetime "sponges" of entanglement, which map to classical percolation theory and allow us to infer values of critical points on our phase diagrams' boundaries.
summary: - Measurement‑only dynamics on hyperbolic lattices reveal an “archipelago” phase of separated symmetry‑protected topological
